paper.title: Scalable Thompson Sampling using Sparse Gaussian Process Models

settings.name_in_paper: Batch sequential optimization of f in an RKHS with noisy evaluations (strict regret)
unmapped: Each round the learner queries a batch of B_batch points; regret summed over all T*B_batch queries
settings.definition_quote: We consider the sequential optimization of an unknown function $f$ over a compact set $\X\subset \Rr^d$. A sequential learning policy selects a batch of $B$ observation points $\{x_{t,b}\}_{b\in [B]}$ at each time step $t=1,2,\dots,T$ and receives the corresponding real-valued and noisy rewards ... Given an RKHS $H_k$, the norm of the objective function is bounded: $||f||_{H_k}\le \Bc$, for some $\Bc>0$, and $k(x,x')\le 1$

algorithms.name: S-GP-TS (batch Thompson sampling with approximate / sparse variational GP and decoupled sampling)

symbols.a_bar: upper multiplicative approximation constant of the posterior std (Assumption 3)
symbols.eps_approx: additive approximation error bound epsilon of the posterior std (Assumption 3)
symbols.alpha_T: covariance scaling 2*u_T(1/T^2) with u_t = a_under_t(S + R sqrt(2(gamma_{tB}+1+log(1/delta))) + c_t)

conditions: Assumption 3 (quality of approximate std) and Assumption 4 (quality of approximate mean) hold
Assumption 5: discretization D_t with |f(x)-f(x^(t))| <= 1/t^2 and |D_t| <= C(d,B) t^{2d}

source.label: The:RegretBoundsApproximate
source.quote: Consider S-GP-TS with $\alpha_t = 2\u_{t}(1/(t^2))$. Under Assumptions~\ref{AssNoise},~\ref{AssNorm},~\ref{Ass1}~,~\ref{Ass2} and~\ref{AssDisc}, the regret defined in~\eqref{eq:regdef}, satisfies R(T,B;f) \le 30\bar{a}\beta_TB\sqrt{\frac{2T\gamma_T}{\log(1+\frac{1}{\tau})}}+(31\beta_T+\alpha_T)\epsilon TB + 15B\Bc+2B

results.notes: Holds for any approximate GP model satisfying Assumptions 3-4 (agnostic to sampling rule). Paper's B is batch size (renamed B_batch); paper's \mathcal{B} is RKHS norm bound S. Regret is defined via f values in expectation, hence pseudo_regret.

symbols.gamma_TB: maximal information gain after T*B_batch observations

results.notes: Order form of the same Theorem 1 bound. R is the sub-Gaussian parameter (sigma).

symbols.gamma_TB: maximal information gain after T*B_batch observations

conditions: Matern kernel (nu > d/2, sufficiently larger for inducing points) or SE kernel
Mercer decomposition of kernel used; inducing points from epsilon_0-close k-DPP (rule with inducing points)
tuning: Matern, inducing points: m_t ~ T^{2d/(2nu-d)}, M ~ T^{(2nu+d)d/(2(2nu-d)nu)}
Matern, inducing features: m_t ~ T^{d/(2nu)}, M ~ T^{(2nu+d)d/(4nu^2)}

source.label: The:MatSE
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{AssNoise} and \ref{AssNorm}, with the algorithmic parameters, kernels and sampling rules specified in Table \ref{Table:CC}, S-GP-TS offers $R(T,B;f) = O(B\sqrt{\gamma_T\gamma_{TB}T\log(T)}).$

results.notes: With B=1 recovers exact GP-TS rate. Algorithmic parameters depend on T, hence known horizon.

cited_results.setting_description: Kernelized bandit, f in RKHS with bounded norm, sub-Gaussian noise, sequential (B=1), exact GP Thompson sampling
